doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Bringing Johnny Dodds and Mutt Carey to Chicago
summary: Billy and Mary recall the four-piece group they brought north: Little Mac Robinson on drums, Steve Lewis on piano, Johnny Dodds on clarinet and Mutt Carey on cornet, and the first jazz band put on the stage rather than in the pit.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Johnny Dodds and- Well, that's what I wanted to hear about. Mud Carey told me he came up to Chicago with you.
Yes, yes. And the drummer was Little Mac, Mud Carey on the trumpet. What was his last name? Do you remember? I think his last name was Robinson, but did we call him? Robinson. Yes. Little Mac

Robinson. There was once a Mac Murray there. Yeah. And then I've heard of a Mac Hill that Lee Collins has told me about. It wouldn't be Mac Hill. Oh, no, no, no, no. I didn't know any of those fellas myself, personally. Well, they all were kids. But Roberts. You think it was Mac Robertson? I think
it was Mac Robertson because- Or Robinson or Robertson? Robinson. Robinson.

Yeah, if I'm not sure. Because we'd call him Little Mac. Little Mac, yes. I've heard him call. Yeah. And then we had Steve Lewis. On piano. Yes. Steve Lewis was on piano. Johnny Dodds on clarinet, and Mud Carey on the cornet. Well, who was a trombone player? Well, at that time, he only brought four. That's what Mud told me. Only four pieces that you came up. And we were the first company that had the jazz band on the stage, isn't it? That's right, yes. On the stage. Not down in the pit, we put them on the stage. Oh, you did? I didn't know. That's where it was. Right here at the Monogram Theater. About what year?
